correctness.rationale: The fourth autocorrelation alone determines fourth powers of all Fourier magnitudes and all quadruple zero-sum products; reality converts them to Freiman two-relations on S. The strict 3|D|<|H| bound makes two- and three-step increments well-defined and multiplicative. The sign compatibility c^2=delta(2s0) extends the character from H to K. Fourier inversion yields a translation. A direct 6-point complex-coefficient construction has equal quartic products but noncharacter phase ratio, proving failure at the boundary. Exhaustive checks of 9,573,819 translation intersections and all boundary products passed; finite tests are supplementary only.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 index-two Fourier-support result uses all autocorrelation orders up through six, whereas this theorem uses the fourth order alone for all real signals with strictly fewer than one-third arbitrary spectral holes, with a universal sharp boundary. The closest earlier complete-coset result does not admit holes. Accessible prior primary texts and published-finding corpus did not establish the same theorem; possible broad Freiman-extension coverage remains a material risk.
residual_risks: An older deterministic Freiman two-homomorphism extension theorem for very dense subsets may imply the combinatorial lemma without using autocorrelation language; publication priority needs specialist examination.
The directly cited published Z_6 ambiguity is not itself new; the originality claim is restricted to the positive strict-density fourth-order reconstruction theorem.
No independent expert literature audit has been performed.

value.rationale: A natural exact inverse problem is resolved by a uniform, support-pattern-independent erasure density bound with provably optimal universal threshold. Unlike the general upper bound of sixth order, a single fourth-order correlation suffices on a quantitatively specified large family, and the Z_6 boundary explains the strict cutoff. No downstream publication scale or noise stability is claimed.
